title: Make illegal states unrepresentable
summary: Design types so that nonsense cannot even be constructed, and the compiler checks your rules.

steps.title: Flags that contradict each other
body: How many states can this hold? 2 × 2 × 2 × (null or not) = 16. How many make sense? Maybe 4. Nothing stops `IsCancelled = true, IsShipped = true, TrackingNumber = null`. Every method must defensively check combinations, and someone will forget.
Better: design the type so the bad combinations **cannot be written**.

steps.prompt: Which combination of the fields above is nonsense but still allowed?
options: Shipped but not paid, with no tracking number
Paid, shipped, with a tracking number

steps.title: One status, data where it belongs
body: Replace the flags with one state, and attach data only to the state that has it:
record Shipped(DateTime At, string TrackingNumber) : OrderState;
Now "shipped without a tracking number" does not compile. And `switch` expressions read naturally:

code: OrderState[] states = { new Pending(), new Shipped("ZX9"), new Cancelled("out of stock") };

steps.title: Smart constructors
body: Some rules are about values, not combinations: "a percentage is 0 to 100", "a quantity is at least 1". Put the rule in the type's constructor and the rest of the code can **trust** it:
void AddToCart(Product p, Quantity q)    // no check needed: q is always >= 1
Validation happens once, at the edge, instead of in every method that receives an `int`.

steps.prompt: Can this type hold an illegal state?
items: `bool isLoggedIn; string? userName` (logged in, no name)
`DateTime start, end` with no check (end before start)
`DateRange` whose constructor rejects end before start

steps.title: Kill the flags
prompt: `Connection` uses two flags and a nullable string; the tests found `IsConnected = false` with a `SessionId` still set. Replace it with states:
- `static class Status` with `static string Describe(ConnectionState s)` returning `offline`, `connecting (attempt 2)` or `online as abc`
solution: public static string Describe(ConnectionState s) => s switch
template: Dojo.Check("Disconnected carries no session", typeof(Disconnected).GetProperty("SessionId") == null, "Disconnected still has a SessionId");

steps.title: A type that refuses nonsense
prompt: - a constructor `DateRange(DateOnly start, DateOnly end)` that throws `ArgumentException` when `end` is before `start`
- `int Days` = number of days including both ends (`End.DayNumber - Start.DayNumber + 1`)
- `bool Overlaps(DateRange other)`: true when the two ranges share at least one day (both ends count, so Jan 1-31 and Jan 31-Feb 5 overlap)
solution: if (end < start) throw new ArgumentException("end is before start");
public bool Overlaps(DateRange other) => Start <= other.End && other.Start <= End;
template: var dojoJan = new DateRange(new DateOnly(2025, 1, 1), new DateOnly(2025, 1, 31));
Dojo.Eq("a one-day range", 1, new DateRange(new DateOnly(2025, 3, 3), new DateOnly(2025, 3, 3)).Days);
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("end before start is refused", () => new DateRange(new DateOnly(2025, 2, 2), new DateOnly(2025, 2, 1)));
Dojo.Eq("overlapping ranges", true, dojoJan.Overlaps(new DateRange(new DateOnly(2025, 1, 31), new DateOnly(2025, 2, 5))));
Dojo.Eq("separate ranges", false, dojoJan.Overlaps(new DateRange(new DateOnly(2025, 2, 1), new DateOnly(2025, 2, 5))));
